summary.headline: H1 FY27 PAT rose 25% to Rs 4.72 crore on sales of Rs 24.94 crore, with IML profit up 39% offsetting a 19% fall in End Caps profit.
summary.overview: Dhaval Packaging's first results call after its BSE SME listing on 6 August 2026 covered H1 FY27 (April–September 2026). Revenue was broadly flat at Rs 24.94 crore versus Rs 34.64 crore last year, while EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 7.83 crore and PAT rose 25% to Rs 4.72 crore. Growth came from the IML business, where margins improved on granule purchasing and pass-through pricing; End Caps weakened on Middle East disruption. Management flagged a rise in receivables to about Rs 13 crore and pointed to a new metal packaging line due by March 2027 as the next growth lever.

segments.name: IML (In-Mold Labelling) and other plastic products
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 26.01 crore (up ~4% YoY) and profit Rs 5.78 crore (up 39%), helped by bulk granule purchases at lower prices and pass-through of price hikes to customers. Serves FMCG and ice cream clients including ITC, Vadilal, Havmor and Sheetal.

segments.name: End Caps
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 8.79 crore (down ~7% YoY) and profit Rs 2.47 crore (down ~19%). Demand hit by Middle East conflict and higher container freight rates that stalled SAW pipe output at customers; sequential sales up ~8%.

segments.name: Filling machines (new)
segments.commentary: First sales of about Rs 14 lakh, sourced from China and tested with customers; positioned to serve IML clients and as a precursor to metal packaging.

segments.name: Metal packaging (upcoming)
segments.commentary: Planned two-piece DRD cans, described as a first in India; machines ordered and lines targeted by March 2027. Management guided to higher margins than IML, but gave no figures.

guidance_outlook: New facility about 75–80% complete and ready for use by March 2027.
Management expects 35–40% revenue increase from the metal packaging line, cited for Q1 FY28 in one answer and for H1/H2 FY27 in another; the wording was inconsistent.
Expects metal packaging margins to be higher than current IML margins; no numbers given.
Expects IML volumes in Jan–June 2027 to be well above last year, with Vadilal contract expected; Q4 to exceed last year's Q4.
Possible IML projects from Latin America and UK clients needing 4–6 machines running 365 days; timing not committed.
Declined to predict FY28 or the next three years until H1 FY28 numbers are visible.
capex_capacity: New plant and buildings under construction; completion targeted by March 2027.
Machines for the metal packaging line already ordered; new packaging lines are planned for the new capacity.
IML capacity is at or near optimum utilisation; additional machines are waiting for the new facility, with rented premises an option if overseas IML orders firm up.
Management said the IPO proceeds will be deployed as promised in the offer document; no split was given.
IPO raised about Rs 36.30 crore (37,48,800 shares at Rs 97).
demand_pricing: IML price hikes of about Rs 23 per unit were accepted by customers in the festive season; management said input cost increases are fully passed through.
Granules are bought in bulk from outside India at prices management says are below domestic competitors'.

End Caps demand is constrained by the Middle East conflict and container freight costs; the company cites Saudi and UAE enquiries but says they are stalled. It is also looking at US and Australian markets.
Top 10 customers account for about 55–60% of revenue.
Receivables rose to about Rs 13 crore as Diwali-linked IML sales were collected more slowly than usual.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timeline of the new facility, and what revenue will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Facility is about 75–80% complete and will be ready by March 2027. Management expects a 35–40% revenue increase from the metal line, initially framed as Q1 FY27 and later as H1/H2.

qa_highlights.question: How is End Caps performing given the Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and container rate increases have stopped SAW pipe producers from producing and shipping. Management hopes conditions improve and points to US and Australian leads.

qa_highlights.question: Can raw material cost inflation from the war be passed to customers in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IML is a relationship business with a 25-year customer base. It said bulk purchasing gave lower prices and that the Rs 23 hike was accepted, with no margin hit expected over the next three months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook for IML and End Caps, and what contribution is expected from the new facility in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: End Caps recovery depends on Middle East normalisation. Management declined to forecast FY28, saying it would plan after H1 FY28 results.

qa_highlights.question: What margin is expected from the new metal line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins above IML because it is a first-of-kind product in India, but gave no figures and will update at FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the top 10 customers and what share of revenue do they make up?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers make up about 55–60% of revenue. The company said the customer list had been published but it would check before naming them.

risks_watch: Receivables rose from about Rs 8 crore to about Rs 13 crore, which cut operating cash flow. Watch collection days after Diwali.
End Caps is still under pressure from Middle East conflict and freight rates. Watch whether sequential recovery holds.
The metal packaging line and the new plant depend on the March 2027 commissioning date. Timing and ramp-up are unproven.
Revenue projections (35–40% uplift) were given inconsistently across answers, and no margin numbers were given. Watch for clarity in the next quarter.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are 55–60% of revenue.
Segment disclosure is limited; management was asked to publish IML and End Caps figures half-yearly, which it did not confirm.
summary.management_tone: Confident on IML and the metal packaging opportunity, but cautious and somewhat evasive on End Caps timing, FY28 and receivables. Management repeatedly deferred to external factors and declined to give forward numbers beyond March 2027. Several answers were disorganised.
key_quotes: Our sales were steady, but our profits grew much faster.
We are not bearing it at all.
We are looking higher profit margin compared to the IML what we are getting right now.

growth.why: Management guides 35-40% revenue uplift from the metal packaging line, but timing is inconsistent (Q1 FY28 in one answer, H1/H2 FY27 in another) and the new plant is only 75-80% complete for March 2027; the Vadilal IML contract and Q4 volume expectations add support, but no margin figures were given.

quality.why: Reported H1 FY27 revenue was down (Rs 24.94 cr vs Rs 34.64 cr), so there is no headline growth to explain; profit growth (PAT +25%, IML profit +39%) came mainly from IML margins on cheaper bulk granule purchases and pass-through of a Rs 23/unit price hike, while IML sales rose only ~4% and End Caps sales fell ~7%. The brief discloses no one-off gains or losses, but the profit rise depends on input

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: IML margins rose on cheap bulk granules and full pass-through of Rs 23/unit price hikes, and metal packaging is guided above IML margins, but no figures were given and End Caps profit fell 19% (Rs 2.47 crore).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New facility is 75-80% complete and due by March 2027, and metal packaging machines are already ordered, so new capacity should come live around the end of the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Jan-June 2027 IML volumes well above last year, with a Vadilal contract and Q4 above last year's Q4, and guides a 35-40% revenue uplift from the metal line, though timing is inconsistent.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: IML capacity is at or near optimum utilisation, additional machines are waiting on the new facility, and rented premises are an option if overseas orders firm up (Latin America and UK projects needing 4-6 machines).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it will update at FY27 and has guided a 35-40% revenue uplift from the metal line, but declined to forecast FY28 and gave no margin figures.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables rose from about Rs 8 crore to about Rs 13 crore, End Caps is stalled by Middle East freight costs, and the metal line timing is inconsistent between Q1 FY28 and H1/H2 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two-piece DRD metal cans, described as a first in India, have machines ordered and lines targeted by March 2027, and filling machines (about Rs 14 lakh sold) are being tested with customers.

rows.label: Latin America and UK IML projects
rows.why: Possible projects needing 4-6 machines running 365 days, but timing is not committed and they depend on rented premises if orders firm up.

rows.label: End Caps recovery via Middle East normalisation or US/Australia leads
rows.why: End Caps sales are down 7% YoY at Rs 8.79 crore and profit down 19%, with Saudi and UAE enquiries stalled, so recovery depends on conditions outside the company's control.

rows.label: Receivables normalisation after Diwali
rows.why: Receivables rose from about Rs 8 crore to about Rs 13 crore as Diwali-linked IML sales were collected slowly, and the company has not committed to a collection timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on IML pricing pass-through and the metal packaging opportunity but cautious and evasive on End Caps timing, receivables and FY28, with inconsistent timing on the 35-40% revenue uplift; analysts pressed on the timeline and margin figures.
